assessments.reasoning: The feature-present branch refers to the serialized-result rules, whereas the feature-absent branch requires fn:serialize and specifically prohibits error on reading an output declaration, with an invocation-error caveat.

challenge.method: Compare absence of a standard serialization interface, reading a declaration, invoking fn:serialize, and vendor-defined serialization under the exact feature clauses.
challenge.results: A processor can omit the standardized result interface and still owes a fn:serialize implementation. The invocation caveat does not permit failing merely because an output declaration was read without the feature. Vendor-defined serialization is outside the standardized feature.

limitations: The source is the exact acquired W3C edition identified by the evidence record. The observed 2021 metadata notice and independently inspected linked context do not supply a different normative edition.
This claim does not assert successful invocation, a particular result interface or equivalent behavior in other versions.
